content.text:
**Bun v1.4** is the latest major release (August 20, 2026) of Bun, a fast all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript runtime, package manager, test runner, and bundler designed as a drop-in replacement for Node.js.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### Major Highlights
- **Rust Rewrite**: The core of Bun (previously written in Zig) has been completely rewritten in Rust — about 1 million lines — while keeping the JavaScript engine (JavaScriptCore/WebKit) unchanged. This is the first release built in Rust; 1.3.14 was the last Zig-based version. The rewrite improves memory safety, compile-time bug detection, and maintainability, with benchmarks matching or beating the previous version and a ~20% smaller binary.[[2]](https://gihyo.jp/article/2026/08/bun-1.4)

- **Node.js Compatibility**: The biggest jump since Bun 1.0 — **+1,517** passing tests from the Node.js test suite. Many core modules (`node:http`, `node:fs`, `node:cluster`, etc.) now pass 97–100% of Node's own tests. This enables better support for frameworks like Next.js 16, Playwright, Vitest, and OpenTelemetry. Bun now reports as Node.js 26.[[3]](https://appwrite.io/blog/post/announcing-bun-1-4-runtime)

- **Performance Improvements**:
  - Idle CPU usage reduced by up to **5x**.
  - Memory usage cut by up to **35–48%** (e.g., HTTP servers).
  - Startup time **50% faster** on Linux (hello-world in ~5.1 ms vs. 10.9 ms in 1.3; Node 26 is ~27 ms) and up to 2.5x faster on Windows.
  - Many JavaScript operations are significantly faster (e.g., `new URL()` 4.6×, `marked.parse()` 138×, `Buffer.from("hex")` 8×, Promises 1.5–2.4×, source map decoding 3.1×).[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i38DgEuaJwM)

- **New Built-in APIs** (replacing many npm dependencies and reducing supply-chain risks):
  - `Bun.Image` — Fast image processing (faster than Sharp).
  - `Bun.WebView` — Headless browser automation (uses system WebKit on macOS or Chrome/Edge via CDP; no Puppeteer/Playwright needed). Supports navigation, clicks, JS evaluation, screenshots.
  - `Bun.markdown` — Native Markdown parsing/rendering (much faster than libraries like Marked).
  - `Bun.cron()` — Built-in cron job scheduling.
  - `Bun.Terminal` — PTY (pseudo-terminal) support.
  - Native `Bun.JSON5`, improved streams (`ReadableStream`, etc.), Compression/Decompression streams, and ~3× faster `bun:ffi`.
  - Other CLI additions: `bun run --parallel`, `bun test --parallel`, `bun audit fix`, `bun dedupe`, `bun prune`.[[5]](https://www.stork.ai/blog/bun-14-the-update-that-kills-your-dependencies)

- **Bundler & Build Improvements**: `bun build --compile --target=browser` can now produce a single self-contained HTML file (with JS, CSS, images, etc., inlined). The React compiler is built-in and over 19× faster than via Babel. Better tree-shaking, minification, CSS handling, and TypeScript support.[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i38DgEuaJwM)

- **Production & Runtime Enhancements**: Switched to a single mimalloc allocator with optimizations (scavenger thread, partial page clearing). Experimental HTTP/2 & HTTP/3 support in `Bun.serve()` and `fetch()`. Better Windows ARM64 support, directory serving, Range requests, and more.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### How to Install or Upgrade
```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```
Or upgrade an existing install:
```bash
bun upgrade
```

Official release notes: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4

Bun 1.4 focuses on making JavaScript development more efficient by providing a richer standard library, higher Node compatibility, better performance, and a more maintainable codebase. The Rust rewrite generated some community discussion, but the release emphasizes stability (full test suite passing with no skipped tests).[[6]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-finally-ships-the-rust-rewrite-drama-isn-t-over--fdy7op2yl)

For full details, check the official blog post or the Bun documentation at bun.com.
